name_choice: Kept the design's xpulpf16alt / xpulpfvec: xpulp<subset> style of the PULP 22 branch (xpulpabs, xpulpvect, ...) and the fork's xpulpv; named after GCC's Xf16alt/Xfvec; end in a letter so the ISA parser reads no version (xpulpf16alt2 -> 'unsupported version number 2'); distinct from Snitch xfalthalf/xfvechalf/xfvecalthalf. Version 1.0 like CORE-V and the 22-branch vendor extensions.
implications: xpulpf16alt -> zfinx; xpulpfvec -> xpulpv, zfinx (vfcpka.h.s reads f32 from GPRs); xgap9 -> xpulpv, zfinx, zhinx(+zhinxmin), xpulpf16alt, xpulpfvec. No Snitch xf* extension implied either way; Snitch instructions are predicated only on their own HasExtXf* (no Zhinx/Zfinx predicate), so xgap9 enables none.

GAP9 GCC defines no __riscv_zhinx / fp16 feature macros for xgap9; clang now defines __riscv_zhinx, __riscv_zhinxmin, __riscv_xpulpf16alt, __riscv_xpulpfvec. Harmless (SDK tests none of them), but a difference from GCC.

The new extensions have no instructions yet: -march=..._xpulpf16alt / _xpulpfvec do not make llvm-mc accept .ah or vf* GAP9 instructions until design task T2; __bf16 is still promoted through f32 (T3/T4).
